properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, second half of his CAP question. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-is-reflow2-itself-a-cp-store-behind-an-ap-record`, deliberately kept apart: that one asks whether CAP describes reflow2's OWN architecture. This one asks whether CAP is vocabulary reflow2 should HAND ITS USERS. One node holding both could only ever be half-answered.

SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATE, OF `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` (proposed, 2026-08-08). That node asks about the DIRECTION of inference — should the quality attribute drive allocation rather than be read off it. This asks whether a SPECIFIC well-known trade-off frame belongs in the vocabulary at all. Related, and the answers could differ: the ility→graph direction could be built without CAP ever appearing, and CAP could be added without changing allocation.

⭐ THE CONCRETE GAP, checked rather than asserted. `schema/dimensions.yaml` already carries NINE axes attachable to any node: reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling, maturity. **Consistency is not among them. Availability is not among them. Partition tolerance is not among them.** For a tool whose owner's stated operating context includes federated, independently-evolving systems, that is a real absence rather than a stylistic one.

AND ONE PIECE ALREADY EXISTS UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME: `cap:seam-incompatibility` — "say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary" — is, structurally, a consistency check across a partition between two independently-evolving replicas. The federation work (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:composed-analysis`, `cap:complementary-pairing`) is a distributed-design problem that has never been described in distributed-systems terms.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. CAP is domain knowledge the AGENT brings to a conversation, not vocabulary the graph must hold. An agent can already reason about it and record the resulting decision as an ordinary Decision node, today, with no change whatsoever. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis this has to beat.

B — ADD `consistency` AND `availability` TO THE DIMENSION ENUM. Cheap, additive, existing graphs unaffected. `ility_report` already reports NOT INFORMED with a reason for axes it cannot compute — so honest silence is the built-in default and nothing pretends. NOTE: a new enum value moves NO stamp count, which would be the fifth recorded instance of the stamp being blind to a real compatibility event.

C — ASK IT UPFRONT, at genesis or adopt: "is this system CP or AP under partition, and L or C in normal operation?" This is exactly the shape `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` argues for in Anthony's own words — "if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed." A CAP posture chosen late is a rewrite; chosen early it is a constraint everything else obeys.

D — A CONTRADICTION DETECTOR, and the only option where anything COMPUTES. A design asserting strict consistency AND high availability across a declared partition boundary is claiming something the theorem forbids. reflow2 already has the machinery: `CONTRADICTS`, `cap:kpp` for inviolable intent, `constrains`, and `cap:key-interfaces` for computing whether a change crosses a published boundary. This is a KPP breach with a known proof.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST ONE — reflow2 IS DOMAIN-NEUTRAL AND CAP IS NOT. Its stated operating breadth is greenfield and brownfield and continual, across several organisations; the owner's own context is Space Force systems engineering and a Brookhaven beamline stack. CAP is meaningless for a beamline's mechanical design or a spacecraft thermal budget. Building a distributed-systems theorem into the core vocabulary privileges software architecture over every other domain the tool claims to serve.

⚠️ 2. "PICK TWO OF THREE" IS ITSELF A MISLEADING FRAME, and shipping it would propagate the misreading. CAP forces a choice ONLY DURING a partition; in normal operation a system need not sacrifice either. That is precisely why PACELC exists. A tool that offers CAP as a first-class axis would be handing users the version practitioners most often get wrong.

⚠️ 3. VOCABULARY NOBODY USES IS THE SHAPE THIS PROJECT SPENT A MONTH REMOVING. Requirement's five-state lifecycle runs 3-of-5 unused; BL-198 was the removal work. Nine dimensions already exist and the ility report cannot inform four of them. Two more unused axes make the enum longer and the design no truer.

⚠️ 4. A PLANNED CAPABILITY COSTS THREE GAPS FOREVER (`dec:exploratory-staging`, measured: 34 of 73 open gaps came from routing wishes to Capability). Option D as a planned capability is a standing tax until someone builds it.

📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, narrower than "add CAP": not as a general axis, but where reflow2 ALREADY has the substrate — the federation seam. `cap:seam-incompatibility` computes disagreement between two independently-evolving designs, which is a consistency question with a real detector behind it. If any of this earns its place, that is the door, and it needs no enum change at all.
properties.name: PARKED, NOT ACCEPTED — should consistency/availability/partition-tolerance be vocabulary reflow2 offers? The federation seam is the road if any is ever taken. Anthony, 2026-08-12: revisit later, more important things first.
properties.rationale:
PARKED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-12: "we can add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed, but leave it as not accepted. one day we can come back to this — it doesn't sound like it has huge applicability, so I think there are more important things to deal with in the interim."

WHAT THAT SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It settles the ROAD: if consistency vocabulary is ever taken up, it enters through `cap:seam-incompatibility` — the federation seam, where reflow2 already computes when two independently-evolving designs disagree at a boundary — and NOT as new `dimension` enum values (option B) or a general axis. It does NOT accept the idea, schedule it, or claim it will happen. Status stays `proposed`.

🛑 DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED AS A PLANNED CAPABILITY, and this is the one judgement made on his behalf rather than by his word. He said "add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed" — but `cap:seam-incompatibility` ALREADY EXISTS and is `realized` (it is the built detector this idea would extend), and Capability has no `proposed` status: its lifecycle is planned / in_progress / realized / verified. Creating a NEW planned Capability to hold the idea would cost THREE GAPS FOREVER — unmotivated, unrealized, unverified — which is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s measured finding (34 of 73 open gaps came from exactly that routing). Parking something explicitly because there are MORE IMPORTANT THINGS TO DEAL WITH, and paying a standing three-gap nag for it, would defeat his own stated reason. A proposed Decision is SILENT by construction — `detect_gaps` fires `undecided_decision_point` only on two or more REGISTERED alternatives — so the idea is kept, findable by search, and costs nothing until someone registers real alternatives under it.

IF HE WANTS IT TRACKED AS WORK rather than kept as a thought, that is one `add_capability` call away and the three gaps are the honest price of scheduling it. The choice is his; the default taken here is the quiet one, matching what he asked for.
